newsitem.title: USA: Texaco pipeline break threatens delicate estuary.
newsitem.headline: Texaco pipeline break threatens delicate estuary.

text.p: More than 300 people Monday continued around the clock efforts to clean up about 2,500 barrels of crude oil that leaked near a fragile coastal marsh late Friday, officials said.
An estimated 1,000 barrels of crude from the Texaco Pipeline had been recovered by mid-afternoon Monday, a Coast Guard spokesman told Reuters.

The rupture was in Lake Barre in Terrebonne Parish, about 40 miles southwest of New Orleans. The leak created a seven-mile by two-mile slick, with some ribbons of oil intruding into the marshlands on the lake's northern edge and threatening delicate marsh grasses, authorities said.
The Coast Guard spokesman said shrimpers have been told to avoid the spill area, but oyster harvesting is continuing under a state monitoring system to ensure product safety.

"We have not qualified the impact on our fish, oyster and wildlife resources, but we will continue to monitor and be prepared to respond should any wildlife contamination occur," said Vince Guillory, a marine biologist with the state Department of Wildlife and Fisheries.

Clean-up crews have deployed 29,000 feet of containment boom and 35,000 feet of absorbent boom in the impacted areas, authorities said. More than 64 skimmers and other vessels have been used to recover the spilled crude.
The Coast Guard spokesman said Texaco calculated that 5,000 barrels of crude were unaccounted for, but on-site inspections indicate only 2,500 barrels leaked into the lake.
The 42-mile Texaco pipeline begins at Caillou Island and ends at the Houma, La., station, connecting with the Eugene Island Pipeline System (EIPS), the Coast Guard said.
The 155-mile EIPS, which transports 120,000 barrels of crude oil daily, remained closed as workers tried to repair the Texaco line.
